scan_metadata.notes: Fresh shallow clone of default branch (depth 20), so has_uncommitted_changes reflects the clone (false) not the author's working copy. The repo contains only Markdown docs (README, a design spec and an implementation plan) and a .gitignore; no source code is committed. README says the server is written in Go (go install) and talks to Trilium ETAPI, but none of that code is present, so routes, data access and dependencies could not be inventoried. Go is out of scope for full interface/data-access detection in skill version 1.0. README example config contains the placeholder 'your-etapi-token-here' for TRILIUM_TOKEN and a LAN URL (http://192.168.1.102:8080); this is documentation, not recorded as a source finding.

gitignore_gaps: no .env, *.env, *.pem, *.key or credentials patterns excluded (.gitignore only lists .worktrees/ and the trilium-farmer binary)

proper_secret_handling_found.mechanism: documented design: ETAPI token passed via TRILIUM_TOKEN environment variable in the MCP server config (implementation not present in repo)

interfaces.network_binding: not applicable (stdio transport per README; no code present)

external_apis.host: Trilium Notes ETAPI (URL from TRILIUM_URL; README example http://192.168.1.102:8080)

what_this_app_can_do: Per README and spec only (no code committed): lets Claude Code list, read, search, create and update notes in a Trilium Notes instance through its ETAPI, using a locally spawned stdio process.

data_sources_touched.source: Trilium Notes instance via ETAPI (documented, not implemented in repo)

capability_summary.who_can_reach_it: No server code present. Per README the tool runs as a stdio subprocess of Claude Code, so it is reachable only by the local user running it; it uses a Trilium API token to reach the Trilium host on the network.
unauthorized_action_red_flags: Documented write access (create_note, update_note) to the whole Trilium note tree with a full-access token; the spec describes TRILIUM_ALLOWED_ROOTS and a private-label filter as mitigations, but they cannot be verified because no code is present.
README example uses a plain http:// URL to the Trilium host, so the token would travel unencrypted on the LAN.

top_findings: Repository contains documentation only; no source code to scan
Documented token handled via TRILIUM_TOKEN env var; README example uses a placeholder token and an http:// URL
